title: Anemia

content_markdown:
Anemia is a condition characterized by a reduction in either the number of red blood cells, the amount of hemoglobin, or the hematocrit (percentage of red blood cells in the total blood volume). There are several types of anemia with different causes and treatments. Anemia itself is not a specific disease, but an abnormal condition that causes a decreased amount of oxygen delivered to body tissues, resulting in a variety of potential symptoms.

Common symptoms of anemia include fatigue, weakness, pale skin, unexplained shortness of breath, and heart palpitations. Severe symptoms can include fainting, angina (chest pain), and myocardial infarction (heart attack).

There are several common reasons for anemia in adults, including gastrointestinal (GI) bleeding caused by various gastrointestinal disorders such as peptic ulcers, inflammatory bowel disease, or colorectal cancer; chronic kidney disease; and excessive menstrual bleeding in females.
